questions.q: What does the Get Records element do that Create, Update, and Delete Records don't?
options: It reads data from Salesforce instead of writing to it
It deletes records permanently
It only works in scheduled flows
It runs Apex code directly
questions.explain: Get Records queries an object and retrieves data; the other three data elements write changes to Salesforce.

questions.q: In this lesson's example, why does the Get Decision Maker element query the Opportunity Contact Role object instead of Opportunity?
options: Because Opportunity Contact Role is always faster to query
Because the Decision Maker role isn't stored on the Opportunity itself — it lives on the related Opportunity Contact Role record
Because Opportunity doesn't support filters
Because Get Records can never query the triggering object
questions.explain: The Decision Maker is tracked on Opportunity Contact Role, a related object, not as a field on Opportunity.

questions.q: Why does the Get Decision Maker element need a second condition (Role equals Decision Maker) joined with AND, rather than just filtering on Opportunity ID alone?
options: AND conditions are required by Flow Builder even when unnecessary
Filtering only on Opportunity ID would return every contact role on that opportunity, not just the Decision Maker
The Opportunity ID condition doesn't actually work without a second condition
AND conditions improve query performance but don't change the result
questions.explain: One condition alone returns too many records; the second AND condition narrows the result to the specific role needed.

questions.q: What's the purpose of Sort By and Sort Order when How Many Records to Store is set to 'Only the first record'?
options: They have no effect when only one record is stored
They decide which record counts as 'first' when more than one record matches the filter
They control how fields are displayed in reports
They only matter for Delete Records elements
questions.explain: When multiple records could match the filter, Sort By/Sort Order determine which one becomes the 'first' record that's actually stored.

questions.q: A Get Records element has its 'How Many Records to Store' setting changed from 'Only the first record' to 'All records.' What changes about the variable it produces?
options: Nothing changes — the variable type stays the same either way
The element now produces a collection variable instead of a single-record variable
The element stops applying its filter conditions
The element switches from reading to writing data
questions.explain: 'All records' produces a collection variable, holding every matching record, instead of just one single-record variable.
